note: The twelve axes are shared vocabulary. A traveller rates her comfort 1-5 on each; a destination is rated 1-5 for how much comfort it demands on each. tiers.name: Your first trip should be short, close and arranged.
tiers.summary: Somebody else handles the moving parts, you are back within a few days, and nothing about it is improvised. That is not a lesser trip — it is the trip almost every confident traveller started with.

tiers.name: Your first trip should be planned in advance — and it can be further away.
tiers.summary: With the transport and the stay settled before you leave, distance stops being the hard part. You are readier than you probably think.

tiers.name: You can plan your own trip.
tiers.summary: You would handle most of a journey without help. There are a few things you would rather not deal with, and a well-chosen trip simply avoids them.

tiers.name: You can go almost anywhere and work it out as you go.
tiers.summary: Very little about travelling alone is outside what you are comfortable with. The question is where you want to go, not whether you can.

bookingRules.text: Arrive in daylight. Book the flight or train that lands before dark, and never leave the arrival transfer to chance.
Have the hotel send a car. Pre-arranged pickup costs a little more and removes the worst ten minutes of any trip.
Book a private room in a property with 24-hour reception. A staffed desk at 2am matters more than the decor.
Choose a hotel over a homestay this time. Clearer boundaries, and someone at the desk who is not also your host.
Take the train or fly. Skip the long overnight bus legs — they are where most first trips go wrong.
Hire a car with a driver rather than driving yourself, and agree the route and price before you set off.
Stay in one place and take day trips out. Unpacking once is worth more than seeing one extra town.
Stay somewhere that serves dinner, so eating is never a decision you have to make alone at 9pm.
Check the network before you book. Download offline maps, and carry your bookings on paper as well as your phone.
Avoid shared rooms and group tours for this one. You can add people to a trip later; you cannot remove them.
Book a direct flight, or take the train instead — a connection is one more thing to manage alone.
If you do take a train, book an upper class with reserved seating, and travel in daylight hours.
